# Independent audit of arbitrary simplex parity cores



The parity-shell argument uses only the complete transversal property. A nonempty outside fiber, including one of zero volume, produces a positive-volume integer midpoint with its parity partner; the small total outside mass forces that midpoint into the core. Within a target group the partners are distinct and different from the target. No lattice-emptiness or convex-position hypothesis is hidden in this step.

The row replacement in the determinant proof preserves the determinant, and subtracting half each remaining row's maximum puts all of its entries in the required centered interval. The all-one row has norm \(\sqrt m\), yielding exactly the displayed power of \(m\) and \(2\). The order-statistic exponent \(L=m-J+1\) correctly uses the entrywise bound one for the earlier rows. Both strict margins in (3) hold for every \(d\ge2\).

The normal perturbation estimates in Section 3 are genuinely translation independent. For a maximizer of the unperturbed functional in the partner simplex, its sum with the given small-fiber point lies in \(2T\), so the error is at most \(2\epsilon\). The partner's width is also bounded through this sum inclusion. No separate bound on either partner's position is needed. The actual two cap thresholds sum to twice the middle threshold for every ambient integer tilt. The homothetic-copy dichotomy therefore supplies the same fixed subset credit in every permitted direction.

The balanced centroid shift exists because the barycentric gradients have only their sum-zero relation. Its component and norm estimates have the correct \(m\Gamma V_0\) normalization. The one-positive-vertex cap formula has the correct product denominator, and differentiating it at the centroid yields \(m\Gamma V_0\). The signed integral error is bounded by \(\eta E_w\), including negative threshold increments. Thus the near-direction credit surplus is as stated, without any count-dependent error.

The complementary normal set is compact and excludes all ordinary simplex equality directions. The section-area slab estimate for a simplex in the unit ball controls its translated cap mass. The final smallness conditions imply every earlier bound, ensure the candidate lies in the interior, and depend only on \(d\). Vertical caps retain the whole target fiber. The proof covers every containing closed ambient halfspace after the standard parallel through-point reduction.

The final choice of a target group uses \(E_w\ge E/2^n\); contributions from distinct actual fibers within that one group are added only once. The single continuous normalization at that target multiplies every relevant mass by the same Jacobian and pulls the constructed point and all caps back to the original source. The result is correctly scoped to equal-volume simplex cores with sufficiently small outside mass; it does not claim a universal parity-core concentration theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
